subject: Request: Community HackLab trial top-up for student hackathon
messages:
From: Sophia Liu <sophia@hacklab.org>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Prof. Aaron Whitman <aaron.whitman@stateu.edu>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Community HackLab trial top-up for student hackathon

Hi Tessa,

I'm Sophia — community lead at HackLab, a student-run nonprofit that runs regional hackathons and workshops for undergraduates. We're running a 48-hour in-person hackathon on Dec 4–5 and expect ~220 participants (mix of students and mentors). We used Redwood for last year's workshop demos and the teams loved the latency/perf.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood extend our trial window by ~30 days so teams can finish their final projects after the event?
- Would you be able to provision a promo/credit allocation for model inference and scoring (we use generation for mentors and an automated scoring pipeline for hackathon submissions)? Ballpark request: $1,500–$2,500 in credits, or an equivalent token allocation.

We can provide our nonprofit verification and a short event runbook. Attached: event_schedule.pdf (workshop + judging timeline).

Thanks — really hopeful we can continue to rely on Redwood for our workshops.

Best,
Sophia Liu
Community Lead, HackLab
sophia@hacklab.org

---
Attachment: event_schedule.pdf (PDF, 85KB)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sophia Liu <sophia@hacklab.org>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Community HackLab trial top-up for student hackathon

Hi Sophia — thanks for the note and for the attach. Love what HackLab is doing.

A few quick questions so I can expedite this with our partner credits team:
- Can you share an estimate of expected token usage (workshops vs scoring) and which model families you plan to use?
- Are you a registered 501(c)(3) or otherwise tax-exempt? If so, can you send a copy of the certificate or a sponsor (e.g., StateU) contact?

We can provision a provisional 30-day extension + up to $1,500 in promo credit right away pending partner review. If you can confirm the expected usage and provide the tax docs, I can escalate to Monica and Marcus for approval of an increased allocation (up to $2,000).

Also, if you want a promo code that restricts usage to specific endpoints (e.g., inference only, not embeddings) mention that and we can lock it down.

CCing Monica (partnerships) to keep them in the loop.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Partnerships — Education & Community Programs
Redwood Inference
tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Request: Community HackLab trial top-up for student hackathon

Hi Tessa — thanks for the quick reply. Details below:

Estimated usage (rough):
- Instructor demos/workshops (live sessions across 4 tracks): ~250k tokens total
- Automated scoring for submissions (post-hackathon batch scoring, ~600 projects): ~800k tokens if we run a 2-pass scoring pipeline
- Buffer for troubleshooting + demos: ~100k tokens
Total expected tokens: ~1.15M tokens (mostly over a 2–3 week window around the event).

Model: we'll primarily use an open decoder family similar to redwood-13b (we run locally where possible but want hosted inference for judging and live demos).

Nonprofit status: HackLab is registered as a 501(c)(3) under a fiscal sponsor (State University Foundation). Attached: tax_exemption.pdf and the sponsor contact (Prof. Aaron Whitman).

If helpful, we can restrict the promo code to the inference route and to a set of model names.

Thanks again — attaching the tax doc and the attendee pledge we've had teams sign.

Best,
Sophia

Date: 2026-11-17T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: HackLab provisional credit approval

Tessa / Marcus — after reviewing the ask and the docs from HackLab, I'm comfortable approving a provisional $2,000 promo allocation for the Dec event, with the following guardrails:
- Promo code limited to inference endpoints and the redwood-13b family
- Credit valid for 45 days from issuance (to cover post-event scoring)
- Redwood reserves the right to convert unused credit to a standard promo on the account if usage patterns look anomalous

Please create the promo code under the "Community Outreach" partner tag and route the code to Sophia. Create an internal ticket (HLB-9876) to track usage and outcome; if actual usage exceeds this by >20% we should touch base with the team (Sophia can pay overage or we can evaluate an expansion).

Monica
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
